h1: Sarasinee All Suite Bangkok — spacious suites with rooftop pool, a short walk from BTS Krung Thon Buri and ICONSIAM
intro: On the Thonburi side of Bangkok there are very few places where you can get a proper suite — sofa, kitchenette, city view — without spending hotel-chain money. Sarasinee All Suite Boutique Hotel on Charoen Nakorn Road in Khlong San is one of them. The property offers 74 suites across 8 floors, each with a separate sitting area, a small kitchenette with microwave and fridge, and a flat-screen TV — more apartment than hotel room. BTS Krung Thon Buri (Green Line, Silom) is around 450 metres away on foot, roughly 6 minutes' walk. From that station, take the BTS Gold Line directly to ICONSIAM in a few minutes, or hop on the Silom Line for Silom and Sathorn in one to two stops. A rooftop pool with city views, a free gym, free parking, and 24-hour room service round out the offer. Rooms from about ฿900/night, scored 7.4 from over 1,700 real guest reviews — not a flawless hotel, but a strong value proposition for anyone who wants space on the Thonburi riverside without overpaying.

body.html: Who this hotel is for — Sarasinee All Suite positions itself for travellers who want more floor space than a standard Bangkok hotel room, without paying serviced-apartment prices. Every room is a suite with a sofa, a kitchenette (microwave, electric kettle, fridge), and enough room to actually put a suitcase down and spread out. The profile of real reviewers who recommend it includes: multi-night city visitors who want to heat up food without going out every meal, families who need two sleeping areas or kitchen access for children, business guests who want a proper desk and sofa, and deal-hunters who have realised that ฿900–1,200 for a suite with a rooftop pool in walking distance of the Silom line is genuinely unusual in Bangkok. If you are only in the city for one night or need nothing beyond a clean bed and fast Wi-Fi, the value equation tips — there are simpler options at lower prices nearby, like Hop Inn Krung Thon Buri, right on the BTS.

Location and getting around — the hotel stands at 369 Soi Charoen Nakorn 14/2, Charoen Nakorn Road, Khlong San, Bangkok 10600. This places it on the Thonburi side of the Chao Phraya River, in the Khlong San district — a working neighbourhood with street food, local coffee shops, and a distinctly non-tourist feel. BTS Krung Thon Buri station is approximately 450 metres away, an easy 5–7 minute walk. From Krung Thon Buri station you can board the BTS Gold Line (free, air-conditioned) to Klong San and ICONSIAM in a few minutes, or take the Green Line (Silom route) to Chong Nonsi, Silom, or Sathon in two to three stops. For drivers, there is free self-parking on the hotel grounds. The surrounding streets are lively during the day but carry regular traffic noise — rooms facing the street can be noisier than those at the rear. There are some convenience stores and eateries within walking distance, though the area is not particularly well-stocked with late-night options.
"The room was massive — sofa, kitchenette, proper wardrobe space. Rooftop pool view was lovely. BTS Krung Thon Buri is genuinely a short walk. For the price I couldn't believe how much space I got."

Rooms and facilities — the hotel's 74 rooms sit across 8 floors in four main categories: Suite (twin single beds), 1 Bedroom Suite (double bed), Premier Deluxe Suite (twin beds, larger floor area), and Royale (double bed, some with balcony). All rooms include air conditioning, a flat-screen TV with cable channels, a mini-fridge, a kitchenette with microwave and electric kettle, a sofa lounge area, and a private bathroom. Some rooms have city views or a private balcony. The feature that generates the most consistent positive comment across real reviews is sheer room size: guests repeatedly note it exceeds expectations for the price point. The hotel's public facilities include a rooftop outdoor swimming pool with a sun deck, a free fitness centre, a restaurant, 24-hour room service, a tour desk, free Wi-Fi throughout, and an elevator. One note of caution from real reviewers: the kitchenette, while equipped with appliances, often comes without crockery or cutlery — if you intend to cook or reheat food, plan to buy supplies on arrival.

Service and staff — the front desk operates around the clock, useful for arrivals on late flights or early Chao Phraya boat departures. Check-in is from 14:00; check-out by 12:00. Taxi and transport assistance is available. On the staff experience, real reviews tell a mixed story: a significant number praise front-desk staff as friendly, helpful, and willing to go the extra mile, while a meaningful minority report slow check-in, unfriendly reception encounters, or disputed housekeeping charges. As a boutique independent property, the experience here can depend on which member of staff you meet more than at a hotel chain. The overall picture from 1,700-plus reviews points to service that is adequate to good on most visits, but occasionally inconsistent in ways a chain property would not be.

Honest guest feedback — what people say — the 7.4/10 score on Agoda from over 1,700 reviews tells a nuanced story. What guests consistently praise: the generous room size that makes the price feel like strong value; the kitchenette as a genuine convenience for multi-night stays; the rooftop pool and city views; the free parking as a real draw for road-trippers; and the BTS Krung Thon Buri proximity that opens up the whole Silom-Sathorn corridor. What guests consistently flag: Wi-Fi signal is weak or non-existent in some rooms — this is one of the most repeated complaints and a significant issue if you plan to work remotely; housekeeping quality varies between stays; the single elevator becomes a bottleneck in a busy 8-floor building; water pressure inconsistency in some bathrooms; and the rooftop pool has received comments about maintenance not always being consistent. The kitchenette's lack of cooking utensils is noted often enough to be a pattern rather than an isolated complaint.

Price and value — standard Suite rooms start from approximately ฿900–1,200/night in low-to-mid season, climbing toward ฿1,400–1,800 over long weekends and the high-season window from October to February. For a suite-format hotel with a rooftop pool, free gym, and free parking at less than 500 metres from a BTS station on the Thonburi side of Bangkok, this pricing is widely recognised in real reviews as genuinely competitive. The critical comparison is with standard hotel rooms at similar prices that are half the size and lack the pool and kitchenette — for extended stays, families, or anyone who wants to occasionally cook, Sarasinee offers clear value. Where the calculus shifts is for guests who prioritise reliable Wi-Fi, consistently clean rooms, and service predictability — here, spending ฿300–500 more per night at a chain hotel with stricter quality controls may be the better call.

Bottom line — Sarasinee All Suite Bangkok delivers something rare: a legitimate suite with kitchenette, rooftop pool, free gym, and free parking at under ฿1,500/night, within a 6-minute walk of BTS Krung Thon Buri and a Gold Line ride from ICONSIAM. The 7.4/10 score from real guests reflects a property that punches well on value and location but still has rough edges — weak Wi-Fi in some rooms, uneven housekeeping, and service that lacks the consistency of a chain. Set expectations accordingly and you will likely find the space-to-price ratio hard to beat on the Thonburi riverside. Go in expecting a perfect 5-star and you will be disappointed.

honestSummary: Sarasinee All Suite is worth serious consideration if you want a wide suite with kitchenette, a rooftop pool, free gym and free parking at under ฿1,500/night with a 6-minute walk to BTS Krung Thon Buri and a Gold Line ride to ICONSIAM. Set expectations correctly though — the 7.4/10 from 1,700+ real reviewers signals inconsistent service, variable housekeeping, and patchy Wi-Fi in some rooms. Value per square metre of floor space is a standout; predictability of every service touchpoint is not.
honestChecks: If you need fast, reliable Wi-Fi for remote work or video calls — many real reviews flag weak in-room signal as a genuine problem. Book with a backup data SIM in mind; alternatively, contact the hotel in advance to request a room with a confirmed strong signal.

If you expect the same service standard every visit (as with a hotel chain) — Sarasinee is an independent boutique and reviewers note variability in housekeeping and front-desk responsiveness. Inspect the room on arrival and raise any issues immediately rather than waiting.

If you want to cook using the kitchenette — appliances (microwave, kettle, fridge) are there, but crockery and cutlery often are not. Plan to pick up basic supplies from a nearby convenience store or market when you arrive.

tips.title: Use the BTS Gold Line for ICONSIAM
tips.body: From BTS Krung Thon Buri station (6 min walk from the hotel), board the free Gold Line (BTS Sai Sii Thong) for Klong San and ICONSIAM — a few minutes' ride, no Grab wait, no traffic. Much faster than driving in the afternoon.

tips.title: Bring a backup data SIM
tips.body: In-room Wi-Fi reliability is one of the hotel's most commented-on weaknesses. If you need to work online, stream video, or make video calls reliably, buy a Thai data SIM on arrival (AIS, True, or DTAC all sold at ICONSIAM and major convenience stores).

tips.title: Request a rear-facing room
tips.body: Charoen Nakorn Road carries regular traffic and rooms at the front of the building can be noisy during the day. At check-in, ask for a room facing away from the street — the rear and upper floors tend to be quieter.

tips.title: Stock the kitchenette yourself
tips.body: Microwaves and kettles are provided but plates, cutlery, and sponges typically are not. If you plan to heat food or make instant noodles, stop at a 7-Eleven or local wet market on your way from the BTS to pick up basics. The neighbourhood has morning food stalls worth exploring too.

faq.q: Where is Sarasinee All Suite Bangkok and which BTS station is nearest?
faq.a: The hotel is at 369 Soi Charoen Nakorn 14/2, Charoen Nakorn Road, Khlong San, Bangkok 10600 on the Thonburi side of the Chao Phraya River. The nearest BTS station is Krung Thon Buri (Green Line, Silom route), approximately 450 metres away — around a 5–7 minute walk. From Krung Thon Buri you can board the free BTS Gold Line for direct service to ICONSIAM in a few minutes.

faq.q: How do I get from Sarasinee All Suite to ICONSIAM?
faq.a: Walk about 6 minutes to BTS Krung Thon Buri station, then transfer to the Gold Line (BTS Sai Sii Thong, free) for Klong San and ICONSIAM in two stops — total journey time around 10–12 minutes. Alternatively, a Grab from the hotel to ICONSIAM takes roughly 5–8 minutes depending on traffic.

faq.q: Does Sarasinee All Suite have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes — there is an outdoor rooftop pool with a sun deck and city views, available to all guests. A free fitness centre is also on site. Some real guest reviews note that pool maintenance has been inconsistent at times; check with the hotel on arrival if this is important to your stay.

faq.q: What are the room prices at Sarasinee All Suite Bangkok?
faq.a: Rooms start from approximately ฿900/night for a standard Suite in low-to-mid season. Rates rise toward ฿1,400–1,800 during the October–February high season and long Thai public holidays. The hotel has 74 rooms — book in advance on Agoda or Trip.com and choose free cancellation for flexibility.

faq.q: Do the rooms at Sarasinee All Suite have a kitchen?
faq.a: Every room has a small kitchenette with a microwave, electric kettle, and mini-fridge. However, real guest reviews consistently note that crockery and cutlery are usually not provided — if you intend to heat or prepare food, pick up plates and cutlery from a nearby 7-Eleven or local market. The hotel also has a restaurant and 24-hour room service for meals without cooking.
